_comment: Why NAVCORE-SoOP's pins differ from MatekH743's. The differences themselves are computed by tools/gen_pinmap.py from firmware/reference/MatekH743-hwdef.dat and the generated firmware/NAVCORE_SoOP/hwdef.dat; this file only says why.

board_notes.PA2: PWM5 moved to PB9: PA2 faced the RF corner and its trace could not reach TP3
board_notes.PA4: Q channel of the SoOP receiver (ADC2 ch18), sampled by AP_SoOP, not declared in the hwdef; single battery, so no BATT2
board_notes.PA7: payload 5 V rail switch, GPIO 83 = RELAY1_PIN; single battery, so no BATT2 current
board_notes.PB0/PB1: M1/M2 on TIM3_CH3/CH4, not MatekH743's TIM8_CH2N/CH3N, which cannot run bidirectional DShot; same pins, so stock binaries still drive the motors
board_notes.PB8: PWM7 (TIM4_CH3) to the servo header J17; UART4 is not used, so SERIAL6 is EMPTY
board_notes.PB10/PB11: I2C2 - MS5611 baro @0x77 and the MAX2112 tuner
board_notes.PB6/PB7: I2C1 - external compass on the GPS port J3, plus the off-board rangefinders on J9
board_notes.PB12: MAX7456_CS in MatekH743; no analogue OSD here
board_notes.PB13/PB14/PB15: SPI2 not declared: it served only the analogue OSD, which is not fitted
board_notes.PC2: antenna feed current, from U25 (INA180A2) across the bias tee's sense resistor
board_notes.PC4: I channel of the SoOP receiver (ADC1 ch4), from the OPA2374 difference amp; no airspeed sensor
board_notes.PC5: antenna 5 V feed enable (U24), high from boot
board_notes.PC7: USART6_RX only: the RC timer input (RCININT on TIM3_CH2) is dropped, since RC is CRSF on SERIAL7 and TIM3 drives M1/M2
board_notes.PC13: EXT_CS1, the optical flow chip select on J14; no third IMU
board_notes.PD4: EXT_CS1 moved to PC13, which reaches J14's corner
board_notes.PD10: antenna feed fault flag from U24
board_notes.PD11: FLOW_MOTION, pulled down and not wired: J14 has no pin for it, and ArduPilot's PixArt driver polls over SPI
board_notes.PD14/PD15: PWM9/PWM10 dropped: no connector, and TIM4_CH3/CH4 serve PWM7/PWM5
board_notes.PE1: UART8_TX not declared: UART8 only receives ESC telemetry on J2 pin 8
board_notes.PE2: EXT_CS2 - W25Q128 for the Iridium TLE catalogue

adc_design_note: I/Q reaches the MCU as TWO SINGLE-ENDED channels, not two differential pairs. VERIFIED from ArduPilot hwdef/scripts/STM32H743xx.py: PC4=ch4, PA4=ch18, PA7=ch7, PC5=ch8, and all four exist on BOTH ADC1 and ADC2 - which is what makes dual-simultaneous sampling possible. NOT VERIFIED: the exact INP->INN pairing for differential mode (st.com refused the datasheet download). STM32H7 differential mode uses fixed INP/INN pin pairs rather than arbitrary pin choice, and those INN pins are largely consumed by SPI1 here - so the design avoids ADC differential mode entirely rather than depend on an unconfirmed detail. The OPA2374 is two four-resistor difference amplifiers (Rin 4k7, Rf 10k, gain 2.13, output centred on a 1.65 V reference) with 100 pF across each feedback resistor for a 159 kHz first-order anti-alias corner: the MAX2112's own baseband filter is 4 MHz at its narrowest and the H743 ADC samples below 3.6 MSPS, so without that corner the tuner's noise floor folds into the burst's band. Better regardless of the INN mapping: higher CMRR and half the ADC channels. This block shipped for a long time as 'resistor values TBD by sim' with NO feedback network at all - open-loop comparators - and was completed on 2026-09-17. CRITICAL: sample PC4 on ADC1 and PA4 on ADC2 in DUAL REGULAR SIMULTANEOUS mode - any I/Q sampling skew becomes a phase error, which corrupts the Doppler frequency estimate directly.
